doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Bad experiences on the scene and singers with sidemen
summary: She was occasionally vibed as just the singer but never had bad musical experiences.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: This is a hard question, and I haven’t had much luck with it in the past anyway, did you ever have any really bad gigs or sort of a traumatic experience that in retrospect you learned from, maybe in those jam session scenes.

Well there was a whole lot of you know, well she’s just the singer. You know singers get that. And you know, I never really was too into that. But I never really had any very bad experiences except for being a little bit vibed. Once I started singing people would usually stop vibing me because they realized that I had done my homework, you know what I mean? But yeah I never really had very many bad experiences. When it comes down to music, everything’s been great. It’s been some of the stuff around it that has been bad experiences in my career. But I’ve always had wonderful experiences with the music itself.
Well as a sideman, singers can help the sidemen a lot, or they can hinder the whole process. You know that’s something I guess you learn through experience.
Um hum. I mean the whole thing has to fit together and be right. It does.
